observations: Photo 0 shows a bare automotive engine (block, valve cover, intake manifold, alternator, wiring harness) sitting on a concrete floor.
Green paint markings visible on multiple sections, typical of used/import engine yard marking, not a brand indicator.
No visible manufacturer plate, engine code sticker, or model number legible in the photo.
A person's legs and sandals are visible in the background, no other context items.
No spark plugs, sensors wiring ends, or turbo/manifold completeness can be confirmed; some connectors appear loose or disconnected.

claims.evidence: No origin marking, plate, or paperwork visible in photo 0; claim rests solely on seller's text.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (compression, timing, bearings) not visible externally.
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine running/starting with audible idle sound.

risks.risk: Unknown make/model/displacement means wrong-fit risk for buyer's vehicle.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of engine code stamp or VIN-linked tag, plus photo of any ECU or manifold casting number.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified generic used engine, lowest comparable tier

risks.risk: Missing or damaged ancillary parts (sensors, injectors, turbo if applicable) reduce value.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set showing all sides including rear bellhousing and injector rail.

risks.risk: Claimed 'Korean parts' origin cannot be confirmed; could be any origin or a mixed/rebuilt unit.
risks.proof: Photo of any origin sticker, import customs tag, or seller's sourcing invoice.
risks.if_unproven: origin disregarded in pricing; treated as unverified generic used import

proof_requests: Close-up of the engine code/stamp or casting number on the block.
Video of the engine running or turning over.
Photos from all sides including the rear (bellhousing/flywheel area) and underside.
Any paperwork or origin tag proving the 'Korean parts' sourcing claim.
response.reason: The engine's make, model, and working condition cannot be read from the single photo, and these are the facts that would set even a worst-case price; a readable engine code or running clip is needed before any price can be assigned.
